subject: node:root
label: use fewer bins on the benchmark instances

data.name: use fewer bins on the benchmark instances
data.frame: Nothing is solved yet. A rule must place each arriving item, once and for good, into an open bin or a new bin; it is judged by the bins used relative to the total size, averaged over seeded instances.
assumptions: items must be placed the moment they arrive
a placed item never moves
the rule sees only the current item and the current bin fills

data.name: choice rule
data.frame: Which of the open bins with room the item goes to. No rule is chosen yet.
assumptions: the first bin with room is as good as any other
bins are scanned in opening order
the choice looks only at whether the item fits, not at the room left after it
data.boundary: the whole file (choose_bin (the selection among bins that fit))

data.name: bin state kept
data.frame: What the rule remembers between calls, beyond the bin fills it is given. Nothing is chosen yet.
assumptions: a fill level is all that matters about a bin
nothing needs remembering between items
all open bins are equally available
data.boundary: the whole file (choose_bin, new module-level state and helper functions)

data.name: when to open a bin
data.frame: When the rule opens a new bin instead of using one with room. Nothing is chosen yet.
assumptions: opening a bin is always worse than using one with room
the decision to open depends only on fit
an item never gets a bin of its own on purpose
data.boundary: the whole file (choose_bin (the condition for returning -1))

data.name: use of item statistics
data.frame: Whether the rule uses the sizes of the items seen so far. Nothing is chosen yet.
assumptions: the size distribution is unknown and stays unknown
past items say nothing about future items
large and small items need no different treatment
data.boundary: the whole file (choose_bin, new module-level counters of item sizes, helper functions)

data.name: tie-breaking
data.frame: How the rule decides between bins that serve equally well. Nothing is chosen yet.
assumptions: ties are rare enough not to matter
opening order is a fair tie-breaker
near-equal fits are treated as different
data.boundary: the whole file (choose_bin (the ordering among candidate bins))

data.name: the whole rule (cross-part changes)
data.frame: Rules that decide the choice, the opening and the state together, as one design.
assumptions: each part can be improved on its own
the parts interact only through the bin fills
the best rule is a sum of the best parts
data.boundary: choose_bin and any helper functions or module-level state in the file
